**Surfaced 2026-05-16 by PRINCIPAL during stoa--32b epic capture.** Sibling to stoa--32b.1 + stoa--32b.2. Parent: stoa--32b.

PRINCIPAL declared the discipline in two messages:

> "We are not ready for a handoff yet, we usually have a bunch of compaction events before we consider a new polybius and then it is usually only if we are making changes to the way polybius works. Handoff + compaction works for a long time...we should add that as number 1 on the polybius refresh pattern."

> "Don't forget handoff likely includes multiple beadworks tickets to use as memories. We are setting up so you will have ariadne tools to search all work."

## The discipline

POLYBIUS session lifecycle has three modes, in order of frequency:

1. **Default — handoff + compaction.** Same POLYBIUS session continues across many compactions. The on-disk handoff doc serves as re-paste anchor for post-compaction self-re-orientation. Plus bw tickets accreting as durable memory across the same session lifetime. This is the COMMON case and works for a long time.

2. **New POLYBIUS session.** Reserved for changes to how POLYBIUS itself works — role file edits, discipline canon updates, architectural reframes that the running session cannot internalize organically. RARE relative to (1).

3. **When (2) fires:** previous POLYBIUS authors the handoff (multi-artifact, see below) + sits idle as relay channel indefinitely; new POLYBIUS spins up against the handoff; previous becomes less relevant over time but may retain important info. The decay-not-termination model.

## Handoff is multi-artifact, not single-doc

Today's misframe (mine, mid-session): I drafted a HANDOFF_POLYBIUS_*.md as if the handoff were the doc. PRINCIPAL corrected: handoff is the multi-artifact substrate state, indexed by the doc. Components:

- **Index doc** — high-density narrative + pointers (HANDOFF_POLYBIUS_<date>.md at the-stoa root by current convention)
- **bw tickets** — epic + children + pointer tickets + retrospective tickets; these are the actual memories
- **Retro docs** — docs/sessions/<date>-<slug>--retro.md for sectioned semantic-chunked records
- **Design artifacts** — agents/design/<arc>/design.md + arc directives at substrate/arcs/
- **Commits** — substrate state at HEAD + commit messages as durable trail
- **Role files / disciplines** — MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md + operating-disciplines.md + CAPTAIN envelopes as canonical context any new session inherits via auto-load or activation paste

A POLYBIUS picking up state reads the index THEN walks the linked artifacts as needed. Future: queries the corpus via Ariadne search rather than reading linearly.

## Ariadne-search-ready authoring (forward context)

PRINCIPAL is setting up Ariadne tools for searching all the substrate corpus. Implications for authoring discipline going forward:

- **Titles matter** — bw ticket titles, retro doc titles, commit subjects should be search-friendly: distinct, specific, named-entities, no relying on context to disambiguate.
- **Cross-refs matter** — every artifact should name its related artifacts explicitly (bw ID cross-refs, file paths, commit SHAs). The retro convention's schema already does this; should propagate to ticket bodies + commit messages.
- **Content density matters** — semantic-chunked sections (per the retro schema) make for better vector retrieval than long monolithic prose.
- **Authoring for ingestion is the same as authoring for human re-reading after compaction** — both want self-contained, well-titled, cross-referenced units. The disciplines align.

This is forward-context — doesn't change anything immediately, but should inform the substrate canon as new sections / disciplines get written.

## Deliverables (sketch — DAEDALUS scopes precisely)

1. **MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md — new section** (likely §6 extension or new §N) titled 'POLYBIUS session lifecycle.' Encodes the three modes above + the multi-artifact handoff shape + Ariadne-readiness as forward authoring discipline.
2. **Possibly: cross-ref from operating-disciplines.md** — lifecycle is POLYBIUS-specific but the discipline of 'authoring for both compaction-recovery and corpus-search' applies universally; consider a section there too.
3. **Possibly: handoff doc template** — substrate/templates/handoff-doc-template.md per the durable-substrate-with-short-prompts pattern (§4.5). Slots: engagement-date, prior-handoff cite, live-relay-status, one-paragraph-state, recommendation-menu, load-bearing-context, bw-repo-table, state-shapes-behavior, memories-cite-dont-restate, hygiene-loose-ends, honest-caveats. The morning's HANDOFF_POLYBIUS_2026-05-16.md is the de-facto template.

## Acceptance (probes — VERA scopes precisely)

- A future POLYBIUS reading MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md cold can correctly identify 'we are at a handoff+compaction moment, not a new-session moment' (verified via synthetic scenarios)
- The handoff template covers all the artifact types the current de-facto convention uses (index doc + bw tickets + retro + design + commits + role files)
- Ariadne-readiness authoring discipline named explicitly (titles + cross-refs + content-density + alignment-with-compaction-recovery)

## Out of scope (do NOT do in this arc)

- Building Ariadne tooling itself (separate effort PRINCIPAL is driving; this arc just acknowledges its forward presence)
- Editing existing handoff docs to retroactively fit any new template (the morning's HANDOFF_POLYBIUS_2026-05-16.md is fine as-is)
- Restructuring bw ticket conventions broadly (this arc may suggest authoring-discipline improvements but doesn't reorganize existing tickets)

## §15 honesty

N=1 + PRINCIPAL declaration. PRINCIPAL named the discipline (project-direction authority). Substrate canon goes in; future POLYBIUS-lifecycle events (handoffs + compactions + the rare new-session events) accrete supporting evidence over time per §6.7.1.

## Cross-refs

- stoa--32b (parent epic)
- stoa--32b.1, stoa--32b.2 (siblings — PRINCIPAL-gate + script/agent split)
- docs/sessions/2026-05-16-substrate-update-architecture-reframe--retro.md — load-bearing source for sibling tickets
- HANDOFF_POLYBIUS_2026-05-16.md at the-stoa root — the de-facto template for the multi-artifact handoff shape
- MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §6 — current compact-or-clear recovery section (covers PLINY; doesn't yet cover POLYBIUS lifecycle)

The reframe: 'POLYBIUS' = all currently-active POLYBIUS sessions (user-tier + project-tier at every workspace) + idle relay-channel POLYBIUSes + the substrate they co-author and inherit. The collective IS POLYBIUS; any specific session is one currently-active branch with one specific perspective and recency-of-context profile. Both renderings are defensible; DAEDALUS picks.

The reframe explains structurally:
- Why the substrate corpus matters (long-term memory of the collective)
- Why decay-not-termination is the right relay-channel model (less-recent perspectives are still part of who-POLYBIUS-is)
- Why Ariadne corpus search is the natural next infrastructure step (queryable cross-collective memory)
